NASB.5: 'For your guilt teaches your mouth, And you choose the language of the crafty.
NASB.6: 'Your own mouth condemns you, and not I; And your own lips testify against you.
NASB.7: 'Were you the first man to be born, Or were you brought forth before the hills?
NASB.8: 'Do you hear the secret counsel of God, And limit wisdom to yourself?
NASB.9: 'What do you know that we do not know? [What] do you understand that we do not?
NASB.10: 'Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us, Older than your father.
NASB.11: 'Are the consolations of God too small for you, Even the word [spoken] gently with you?
NASB.12: 'Why does your heart carry you away? And why do your eyes flash,
NASB.13: That you should turn your spirit against God And allow [such] words to go out of your mouth?
NASB.14: 'What is man, that he should be pure, Or he who is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
NASB.15: 'Behold, He puts no trust in His holy ones, And the heavens are not pure in His sight;
NASB.16: How much less one who is detestable and corrupt, Man, who drinks iniquity like water!

NASB.21: 'Sounds of terror are in his ears; While at peace the destroyer comes upon him.
NASB.22: 'He does not believe that he will return from darkness, And he is destined for the sword.
NASB.23: 'He wanders about for food, saying, 'Where is it?' He knows that a day of darkness is at hand.
NASB.24: 'Distress and anguish terrify him, They overpower him like a king ready for the attack,
NASB.25: Because he has stretched out his hand against God And conducts himself arrogantly against the Almighty.
NASB.26: 'He rushes headlong at Him With his massive shield.

NASB.28: 'He has lived in desolate cities, In houses no one would inhabit, Which are destined to become ruins.
NASB.29: 'He will not become rich, nor will his wealth endure; And his grain will not bend down to the ground.
NASB.30: 'He will not escape from darkness; The flame will wither his shoots, And by the breath of His mouth he will go away.
NASB.31: 'Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself; For emptiness will be his reward.
NASB.32: 'It will be accomplished before his time, And his palm branch will not be green.
NASB.33: 'He will drop off his unripe grape like the vine, And will cast off his flower like the olive tree.
NASB.34: 'For the company of the godless is barren, And fire consumes the tents of the corrupt.
NASB.35: 'They conceive mischief and bring forth iniquity, And their mind prepares deception.'

ESV.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
ESV.2: “Should a wise man answer with windy knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind?
ESV.3: Should he argue in unprofitable talk, or in words with which he can do no good?
ESV.4: But you are doing away with the fear of God  and hindering meditation before God.
ESV.5: For your iniquity teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.
ESV.6: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I; your own lips testify against you.
ESV.7: “Are you the first man who was born? Or were you brought forth before the hills?
ESV.8: Have you listened in the council of God? And do you limit wisdom to yourself?
ESV.9: What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not clear to us?
ESV.10: Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us, older than your father.
ESV.11: Are the comforts of God too small for you, or the word that deals gently with you?
ESV.12: Why does your heart carry you away, and why do your eyes flash,
ESV.13: that you turn your spirit against God and bring such words out of your mouth?
ESV.14: What is man, that he can be pure? Or he who is born of a woman, that he can be righteous?
ESV.15: Behold, God  puts no trust in his holy ones, and the heavens are not pure in his sight;
ESV.16: how much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a man who drinks injustice like water!
ESV.17: “I will show you; hear me, and what I have seen I will declare
ESV.18: (what wise men have told, without hiding it from their fathers,
ESV.19: to whom alone the land was given, and no stranger passed among them).
ESV.20: The wicked man writhes in pain all his days, through all the years that are laid up for the ruthless.
ESV.21: Dreadful sounds are in his ears; in prosperity the destroyer will come upon him.
ESV.22: He does not believe that he will return out of darkness, and he is marked for the sword.
ESV.23: He wanders abroad for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’ He knows that a day of darkness is ready at his hand;
ESV.24: distress and anguish terrify him; they prevail against him, like a king ready for battle.
ESV.25: Because he has stretched out his hand against God and defies the Almighty,
ESV.26: running stubbornly against him with a thickly bossed shield;
ESV.27: because he has covered his face with his fat and gathered fat upon his waist
ESV.28: and has lived in desolate cities, in houses that none should inhabit, which were ready to become heaps of ruins;
ESV.29: he will not be rich, and his wealth will not endure, nor will his possessions spread over the earth;
ESV.30: he will not depart from darkness; the flame will dry up his shoots, and by the breath of his mouth he will depart.

ESV.33: He will shake off his unripe grape like the vine, and cast off his blossom like the olive tree.
ESV.34: For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery.
ESV.35: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil, and their womb prepares deceit.”

AMP.1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered [Job] and said,
AMP.2:
"Should a wise man [such as you] utter such windy and vain knowledge [as we have just heard]
And fill himself with the east wind [of withering, parching, and violent accusations]?
AMP.3:
"Should he rebuke and argue with useless talk?
Or with words in which there is no benefit?
AMP.4:
"Indeed, you are doing away with fear,
And you are diminishing meditation before God.
AMP.5:
"For your guilt teaches your mouth,
And you choose [to speak] the language of the crafty and cunning.
AMP.6:
"Your own mouth condemns you, and not I;
Yes, your own lips testify against you.
AMP.7:
"Were you the first man to be born [the original wise man],
Or were you created before the hills?
AMP.8:
"Do you hear the secret counsel of God,
And do you limit [the possession of] wisdom to yourself?
AMP.9:
"What do you know that we do not know?
What do you understand that is not equally clear to us?
AMP.10:
"Among us are both the gray-haired and the aged,
Older than your father.
AMP.11:
"Are the consolations of God [as we have interpreted them to you] too trivial for you,
[Or] were we too gentle toward you [in our first speech] to be effective?
AMP.12:
"Why does your heart carry you away [allowing you to be controlled by emotion]?
And why do your eyes flash [in anger or contempt],
AMP.13:
That you should turn your spirit against God
And let such words [as you have spoken] go out of your mouth?
AMP.14:
"What is man, that he should be pure and clean,
Or he who is born of a woman, that he should be righteous and just?
AMP.15:
"Behold, God puts no trust in His holy ones (angels);
Indeed, the heavens are not pure in His sight—
AMP.16:
How much less [pure and clean is] the one who is repulsive and corrupt,
Man, who drinks unrighteousness and injustice like water!
AMP.17:
"I will tell you, listen to me;
And what I have seen I will also declare;
AMP.18:
What wise men have [freely] told,
And have not hidden [anything passed on to them] from their fathers,
AMP.19:
To whom alone the land was given,
And no stranger passed among them [corrupting the truth].
AMP.20:
"The wicked man writhes with pain all his days,
And numbered are the years stored up for him, the ruthless one.
AMP.21:
"A [dreadful] sound of terrors is in his ears;
While at peace and in a time of prosperity the destroyer comes upon him [the tent of the robber is not at peace].
AMP.22:
"He does not believe that he will return out of the darkness [for fear of being murdered],
And he is destined for the sword [of God's vengeance].
AMP.23:
"He wanders about for food, saying, 'Where is it?'
He knows that the day of darkness and destruction is already at hand.
AMP.24:
"Distress and anxiety terrify him,
They overpower him like a king ready for battle.
AMP.25:
"Because he has stretched out his hand against God
And behaves arrogantly against the Almighty,
AMP.26:
Running and charging headlong against Him
With his ornamented and massive shield;
AMP.27:
For he has covered his face with his fat,
Adding layers of fat to his thighs [giving himself up to pleasures],
AMP.28:
And he has lived in desolate [God-forsaken] cities,
In houses which no one should inhabit,
Which were destined to become heaps [of ruins];
AMP.29:
He will not become rich, nor will his wealth endure;
And his grain will not bend to the earth nor his possessions be extended on the earth.
AMP.30:
"He will not escape from darkness [fleeing disaster];
The flame [of God's wrath] will wither his branch,
And by the blast of His mouth he will go away.
AMP.31:
"Let him not trust in vanity (emptiness, futility) and be led astray;
For emptiness will be his reward [for such living].
AMP.32:
"It will be fulfilled while he still lives,
And his branch will not be green [but shall wither away].
AMP.33:
"He will fail to bring his grapes to maturity [leaving them to wither unnourished] on the vine,
And will cast off blossoms [and fail to bring forth fruit] like the olive tree.
AMP.34:
"For the company of the godless is barren,
And fire consumes the tents of bribery (wrong and injustice).
AMP.35:
"They conceive mischief and bring forth wickedness,
And their inmost soul prepares deceit and fraud."

Your own lips testify against you.

“Were you the first person ever born?

Do you have a monopoly on wisdom?
NLT.9:
What do you know that we don’t?
What do you understand that we do not?
NLT.10:
On our side are aged, gray-haired men
much older than your father!

“Is God’s comfort too little for you?
Is his gentle word not enough?

What has weakened your vision,
NLT.13:
that you turn against God
and say all these evil things?

from those to whom the land was given

and even on good days they fear the attack of the destroyer.

MSG.2:

MSG.9:

"Even if they're the picture of health,
